beat: round two: the twist (twist intro, caller, three twist turns, three star reactions, two-line jab volley, round-two cut and exit)

lineCount.note: 12 lines in each Ex episode (caller included), 11 in the others. Cut announcement and exit counted because they sit inside the round-two section.

headToHead.ours: S-ep05 Tilly (jab to Vex): "Vex, people who watched that also asked for refunds."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #30 player option: "3.85 billion BC, so you can be into existing before it was cool." Also the rival-undercut rule: B steals A's own phrasing and turns it.
headToHead.verdict: Closest to par in the batch. It steals Vex's 'people who watched' formula and lands on 'refunds', Tilly's world. It is answering a jab, not the twist, and Maximilian never reacts to it, so the hit goes nowhere. Near draw on the line; the bar still wins on consequence.

headToHead.ours: S-ep02 Tilly (Rhyme): "Choose one of them and they'll let you go. Choose me and I can't, so the answer is no."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #12 Vera: "Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!" (repeat-then-turn) and Take Me Out's rhyme-as-instruction ('If he's not Mr Right, turn off your light').
headToHead.verdict: Good flaw-leak: her inability to end a call becomes the pitch, turn on the last word. But Maximilian's intro demanded a rhyme on 'Maximilian' and nobody, including Tilly, takes the dare. TMO's rhyme is a rule the audience then sees enforced; ours sets a rule and drops it. Bar wins.

headToHead.ours: S-ep03 Brock (Truth and Lie): "One: a million pushups. Two: I own a chair. Two's a lie. It's a squat rack."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #67 Scott: "I also used to have Barry the Beachball... fell in love with Tracy the Thumback." and #63 Narrator: "It is just paper!"
headToHead.verdict: Brock blowing the game by announcing the lie is exactly Scott-shaped no-guile comedy. The bar then has the narrator state the plain fact. Ours has Vesper say 'Whisper, Brock', a volume note she already gave him in round one, and never guesses. The line is par, the beat around it is not.

headToHead.ours: H2 Prince (Wingman for Sir Quill): "Sir Quill is a true knight. I know, I knighted him. Small fee. He is still paying."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom #56 paired rival options: "Let me ask you this: would an uncool person be giving Vera 50 Monster Dollars right now?" and #78 Fishsticks options.
headToHead.verdict: The Wingman card is our nearest thing to Monster Prom's paired rival pitches, and Prince's line does what #56 does: a pitch that is secretly a status claim and a money ask. Vesper's charmed reaction ('I'd send the fee') follows. The best single twist turn. But the follow-up jab 'Copying in the palace historian. That was a footnote.' has no antecedent and drops it.

headToHead.ours: S-ep04 The Ex: caller "Pixel said I was worth the wait. Then Pixel opened another tab. For two years." then Prince/Dash jabs "Dash, I have seen your open rate. Brave." / "Prince, I opened your message once. Biggest fan you've got."
headToHead.bar: Take Me Out round 2 (VT where friends and family reveal embarrassing details, then a wave of lights) and Love Island's text sting (read aloud, then reaction faces).
headToHead.verdict: Caller line is good and the jab pair is a real exchange. But the TMO reveal is about the contestant and moves the lights; our ex talks only about the star, nobody answers the ex's actual line, Dash speaks to Pixel's ex as if it were his own, Sir Quill reuses his round-one-episode-01 line word for word, and when Pixel demands 'Duel someone. Anyone. Now.' the jab slot goes to two other bots. Bar wins clearly.

headToHead.ours: S-ep01 Nav (jab to Sir Quill): "Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop."
headToHead.bar: Monster Prom narration: "a robot and a vampire sit down at a cafeteria table to not eat..." and #58 "Does... Scott know any other people? Signs are pointing to 'no.'"
headToHead.verdict: Clean, short, in Nav's grammar, undercuts Quill's length right after Vesper flagged it. Par. Quill's retort 'Thou floating bell jar, turn thou left, and go' is an insult, not an undercut of 'full stop', and the volley ends there. Bar wins on the exchange.

doesTheTwistChangeTheGame: Only Wingman and Roast. They force suitors to talk about each other, so those lines could not exist without the card. The Ex twist does not: the caller's line is never answered (ep-01 busy signal, ep-04 'another tab'), Sir Quill's ex line is the same 19 words in both episodes, and Dash talks to Pixel's ex as his own. Truth and Lie promises 'I guess which' and Vesper never guesses. The Rhyme intro dares a rhyme on 'Maximilian' and nobody attempts one. The Motherboard never speaks. In four of the eight episodes the card is a new question, not a new game.
isRoundTwoBigger: No. Round two is smaller than round one: three turns instead of four, the same answer-then-reaction rhythm with the same reaction length, then a single fixed two-line jab volley that never escalates past one exchange and is never acknowledged by the star. Standings move less in round two than in round one in five of eight episodes (ep-03 moves by one point in total). Nothing new happens to the power structure: no pile-on, no frontrunner, no third party who answers back.
doTheSuitorsGoAtEachOther: Only in the two-line jab slot, plus Wingman and Roast turns. Real undercuts of the line just said: ep-01 Nav 'full stop', ep-04 Dash 'opened your message once', ep-05 Tilly 'asked for refunds', ep-06 Prince 'satisfaction survey', H2 Quill 'Thou art a footnote'. Non-undercuts: ep-02 Crumb 'apology nine' (no apology was made), H1 Brock 'nice try! I'm counting it', H2 Prince 'Copying in the palace historian' (no antecedent), ep-05 Vex 'freshly dumped' (repeats her own twist line). The third suitor in every episode is left out of the jabs entirely.

fixNotes.structure: Most flags are star reactions picked from a per-suitor pool by reaction type and tag hit, whose content is a persona habit (recalculating, variant A, shipping it, please, finished my sentence, crown and flip-flops) rather than a reading of the twist line. Selection should require the reaction to reference a word or claim actually present in the line just spoken, or fall back to a reaction keyed to the twist itself. Jab pairs should be chosen from what the star just set up (Pixel's duel order) and must reference the target's twist line.
fixNotes.bank: Sir Quill and Dash need Ex-twist lines written for the star's ex (not their own) that answer the caller's line. Vex and Tilly need lines that actually play Truth and Lie and Roast. Maximilian needs more than one Brings-up-the-past reaction and a cut line that names who is going. Prince needs more round-two exits. Brock needs jabs that undercut a rival's words.
fixNotes.brain: The live model in hybrid-02/ep-01 defaults to one gamer metaphor per Pixel reaction, explains each one, misgenders Pixel, and writes Brock's exit as an ironic shrug in Pixel's vocabulary.

biggestGap: The star's reaction to each twist turn doesn't read the turn. In about half of the 24 twist reactions the star calls back a habit the suitor never showed on air ('third recalculating', 'variant A', 'said please like a threat', 'finished my sentence'). No reaction resolves the card's own game: no guess on Truth and Lie, no verdict on the Maximilian rhyme, the ex never answers. In the bar, the undercut states the plain fact about the line just said ('It is just paper!'). Make each twist reaction either quote a word from the line it answers or settle the card (guess the lie, score the rhyme, let the caller reply), and drop any pool reaction whose callback is not on the page.
structuralChange: Turn the jab slot into a pile-on against the round's frontrunner so round two escalates past round one. After the three twist turns (about 45 s), the star names the turn that landed best in one line of 10 words or fewer that also settles the card: the Truth and Lie guess, the rhyme verdict, or, on caller twists, the ex replying to that suitor. The other two survivors then each fire one jab at that frontrunner, in seating order. Each jab is 10 words or fewer and must reuse a word from the frontrunner's twist line. The frontrunner gets one comeback, and the cut follows at once. That is five lines in about 15 s, replacing today's fixed two-line volley. Round one becomes everyone against the star and round two everyone against the leader, all three suitors speak in the fight, and the window-C bettors see a visible leader under fire before the cut.
pickMakesSense: Round-two cuts mostly match what viewers saw (a cringing reaction then the cut: ep-01 Nav, ep-04 Prince, ep-05 Vex, H1 Brock). Two contradict the screen. In ep-06 Prince got a charmed reaction ('How small a fee') and was cut over Vex, whose reaction was cringing, on a tie broken by a hidden card. In ep-02 Tilly is cut for the best rhyme of the round. With no hint on screen, both read as random until the reveal.
